patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Lightspeed Retail and Medusa share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Lightspeed Retail only if your buying job matches “Retail POS + omnichannel — Basic $89/mo, Core $149 highlighted, Plus $289/mo USD; Lightspe” rather than Medusa's shape. Choose Medusa only if your buying job matches “Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, Scale $299” rather than Lightspeed Retail's shape. Workflow advantage: Lightspeed Retail leans omnichannel-retail; Medusa leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Lightspeed Retail and Medusa share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Lightspeed Retail is Retail POS + omnichannel — Basic $89/mo, Core $149 highlighted, Plus $289/mo USD; Lightspeed Payments ~1.5% card-present; eCommerce on highe; Medusa is Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, Scale $299, Enterprise custom. No GMV tax..
- Company-size focus: Lightspeed Retail (small-business, mid-market) vs Medusa (small-business, mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Lightspeed Retail-leaning omnichannel-retail vs Medusa-leaning —.
- Researched limits: Lightspeed Retail — No free plan or documented self-serve trial — contact sales is the common path; Medusa — Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX.

Limitations — Lightspeed Retail: No free plan or documented self-serve trial — contact sales is the common path; Third-party payment processors may incur a high monthly surcharge versus Lightspeed Payments (~1.5% card-present) — confirm live; Medusa: Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX; Not a WordPress-native plugin path (see WooCommerce).

Poor-fit cases: Lightspeed Retail is a poor fit when that limitation bites: No free plan or documented self-serve trial — contact sales is the common path · Medusa is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX · Avoid Lightspeed Retail if you actually need Medusa's motion (Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, )

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
